heroSub: 9 hand-picked budget Roi Et stays we've already reviewed, ranked by value — all scoring 7.6 and up. From Hop Inn, our best-value pick with clean rooms from ฿500, to M Grand, the top-scored city hotel at 8.8, garden boutiques, a breakfast-included hotel and a whole detached house that's a bargain split across a group. From roughly ฿500–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏯 Can you do Roi Et on a budget — and how do you pick for value?
introHtml: Good news for tight budgets: Roi Et is an Isan town where rooms are cheap to begin with — even the top-scored hotel in town starts in the low hundreds to low thousands of baht. So doing Roi Et on a budget isn't really about "finding cheap" (almost everything here is cheap); it's about picking the best value once you weigh score against price — a clean room with no guesswork, enough reviews to trust, and extras that actually save money, like breakfast included, a balcony in every room, or splitting a house across a group. That's why we've ranked these 9 stays by value, not by raw score: the ones that start cheap yet score well with plenty of reviews come first. Area still matters a little — the city centre around Bueng Phlan Chai has Roi Et Tower, Somdet Park and lakeside food, all walkable; the outer in-town districts (Rob Mueang, Thewaphibal) have easier parking, good for drivers; and the in-town riverside is quieter but still quick into town. This guide rounds up 9 budget Roi Et stays we've already reviewed, all scoring 7.6 and up — each from real guest reviews, with honest pros and cons, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Roi Et has no metro; you get around by car, though the centre is small enough to stroll around Bueng Phlan Chai on foot, and almost all these budget stays have free parking. Stays in the city centre around Bueng Phlan Chai (near Roi Et Tower and Somdet Park) are a short walk or drive from the lake, temples and restaurants, good if you want to explore the town or don't have a car (M Grand, The Capital, YaYa). Stays in the outer in-town districts (Rob Mueang, Thewaphibal, Roi Et-Kalasin Rd) mostly have parking, good for drivers (Hop Inn, The Premium Residence, Mila Garden, Le Park 23, The Rice). The in-town riverside is quieter but still a walk from Bueng Phlan Chai (Rueanrimnam). The areas in this guide: Around Bueng Phlan Chai — the tower, park, lakeside food · Outer in-town — boutique hotels, easy parking · Riverside — quiet, near town.

entries.storyHtml: We open the budget list with our best-value pick in this guide — Hop Inn Roi Et, with rooms from just ฿500, a score of 8.4 and the most reviews in the guide (120, tied with M Grand). The Hop Inn chain's (Erawan Group) strength is that every branch shares the same standard room: clean, simple and reliably what you expect, no guesswork. The 20 sqm rooms sit on Rob Mueang Road in Nuea Mueang, in town and near Roi Et Tower. There's parking. The trade-off: it's a rooms-only hotel with no pool or breakfast, and the rooms are plain by design. Best for budget travellers who want a clean room with no surprises. (We rank it #1 because it pairs a good score with the lowest from-price and the most reviews — the clearest value in the set.)
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Hop Inn is rooms-only with no breakfast — there are restaurants in town within reach. Rooms are identical across branches; ask for a higher floor for more quiet. The Rob Mueang Road location is handy for driving to the town's sights.

entries.storyHtml: If you want the guide's top score at a price that's still light, M Grand Hotel Roi Et takes the top score in this guide — 8.8 from 120 reviews, tied with Hop Inn for the most reviews. It's a city hotel on Hai Sorok Road, central and near Bueng Phlan Chai and Roi Et Tower. Guests consistently praise its clean rooms, comfy beds and value, plus a location that's a quick drive to the town's sights and a stroll around the lake in the evening. There's parking. The trade-off: it's a standard in-town hotel with no pool, and some rates don't include breakfast. Best for travellers who want a well-scored, central stay with easy access to the sights (a small step up from Hop Inn for the top score and a central location).
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you plan to go up Roi Et Tower or stroll around Bueng Phlan Chai in the evening, it's close — just a few minutes by car. Ask for a Deluxe room, which is larger and in better condition than the Superior for a few hundred baht more. Check at booking whether your rate includes breakfast.

It's on Rob Muang Road Soi 1, in town and near the Roi Et National Museum, with clean rooms and family rooms for larger groups. There's parking. (We rank it here because it's cheaper than the guide's average yet gives you a balcony in every room and plenty of reviews.)

entries.storyHtml: For a boutique feel without paying up, Mila Garden is a garden boutique that scores well and is remembered for its atmosphere — 8.6 from 60 reviews, from ฿700. It's a small 18-room stay on Thewaphibal Road; what sets it apart from the usual in-town hotels is that it was built as a garden boutique, with rooms styled better than the price suggests, garden views and blackout curtains for easy sleeping. It's near the water park and aquarium, good with kids. There's parking. The trade-off: it's a small place, popular rooms fill fast, and it sits in an area you'll need a car to get in and out of town from. Best for couples and anyone who wants atmosphere over a plain place to sleep.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the garden feel, ask for a Superior room, which is larger and faces the garden — guests' favourite. With only 18 rooms, book ahead, especially on weekends. It's near the water park and aquarium, good for a family day out.

It's on Tawapiban Road in town; the draw is the villa design in a quiet garden, parking right at your door, Pet Friendly rooms for travellers bringing a pet, and Triple rooms for small families. The trade-off: reviews are still few, and it's a small resort-style place without the facilities of a larger hotel. Best for couples, pet owners and anyone who wants a garden-villa feel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If bringing a pet, request a Pet Friendly room at booking and tell the hotel ahead, as not all rooms accept pets. You can park right at your door, handy for drivers. For a group, choose the Triple room.

entries.storyHtml: Back to the cheapest from-price in the guide, now with a riverside spot — Rueanrimnam Hotel ('Riverside House') is a riverside boutique in town with from-prices of just ฿500, matching Hop Inn, and it's near Bueng Phlan Chai (7.7 from 13 reviews). It's on Charoen Panit Road in town; the draw is the riverside location, quieter than hotels on the main roads yet still within a walk of Bueng Phlan Chai, plus a VIP room much larger than standard for those who want space. The trade-off: reviews are still few, and it's a small in-town stay with basic amenities. Best for travellers who want a quiet riverside spot near the lake on a budget (same price as Hop Inn, but a riverside feel — traded for fewer reviews).
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more space, choose the VIP Room, which is much larger than standard for not much more. The riverside location is quieter than hotels on the main roads, yet still a walk from Bueng Phlan Chai. From-prices in the low hundreds suit budget travellers.

entries.storyHtml: A central location at a friendly price, traded against uneven room condition — The Capital Hotel Roi Et is a city hotel on Suriyadetbamrung Road near Bueng Phlan Chai (7.6 from 20 reviews), from ฿650. The draw is a location within a walk or short drive of Bueng Phlan Chai and the town's sights, with a range of rooms from Single up to Suite. There's parking. The trade-off, per reviews: it's an older-generation hotel with uneven room condition across the building, which keeps the score mid-range. Best for travellers focused on a central location and price who ask for a renovated room at booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated room or a Deluxe at booking, as condition varies across the building. The central location is a walk from Bueng Phlan Chai, good if you want to explore the town. There's parking.

entries.storyHtml: We close with the pick that's a bargain when you come as a group — YaYa Hostel Roi Et. Despite the name 'Hostel', it's actually a whole-house rental: an entire detached house, 3 bedrooms, 3 private bathrooms, 150 sqm, in town and near Bueng Phlan Chai (8.0 from 18 reviews), from ฿1,200 for the whole house. The draw is having the whole house to yourselves, with a kitchen / prep area, a living space and parking — split across a group, the per-head cost is very low. The trade-off: it's a house rental with no hotel services (no 24-hour reception, no breakfast), and you rent the whole house, so it's not suited to solo or couple travellers. We rank it last because it has the highest from-price in the set, but split across 5-6 people it's excellent value. Best for groups of friends and large families who want to stay together.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a whole-house rental, so the more of you there are, the better value — cheaper per head than booking several rooms. There's a kitchen, good if you like to cook. As a house rental with no full-time reception, contact the owner about check-in times in advance. It books direct on Agoda (no detail page on Booking/Trip yet).

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate from-rates for a standard room in the off-peak season and may change by date and season. We recommend checking live prices and comparing all 3 sites before every booking. Scores and highlights in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms; we didn't stay in person. Every stay here scores 7.6 and up but sits in the budget 2-3 star tier, so there are limits that come with the price — budget-chain and house rentals have no breakfast or 24-hour reception, and most have no pool — so read each stay's caveats before booking. YaYa Hostel books direct on Agoda, so it can't be compared across all 3 sites; the other 8 compare across all three. During the Bun Phawet festival (March), the Samma Nam Khuen Peng Seng Prathip festival (Loi Krathong, November) and long weekends, in-town stays fill fast and rates rise, so book ahead. Roi Et has no metro; you get around by car, and stays in the city centre around Bueng Phlan Chai are easiest for those without one. Guide by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Roi Et hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which budget hotel in Roi Et is the best value?
faq.a: By value (score per baht plus reviews you can trust), Hop Inn Roi Et ฿500, scoring 8.4 with the most reviews in the guide (120), is the best value — same clean chain-standard room every time, no guesswork. Next are Rueanrimnam ฿500, a riverside boutique, and The Premium Residence ฿580, with a balcony in every room. The top score in the guide is M Grand Hotel at 8.8 for ฿760, central in town.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Roi Et hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, from roughly ฿500–1,200/night. The cheapest are Hop Inn and Rueanrimnam from ฿500, The Premium Residence ฿580 and The Capital ฿650; boutique and breakfast-included stays run about ฿700 (Mila Garden, The Rice, Le Park 23), and M Grand ฿760; a whole-house rental like YaYa Hostel starts at ฿1,200 (good split across a group). All are approximate off-peak from-prices for a standard room. Rates rise noticeably during festivals and long weekends.

faq.q: ❓ Coming to Roi Et without a car — which budget stay is convenient?
faq.a: Roi Et has no metro and you get around by car, so without one it's easiest to stay in the city centre around Bueng Phlan Chai, within reach of the lake, Roi Et Tower and restaurants — for example M Grand Hotel ฿760, The Capital Hotel ฿650 or YaYa Hostel ฿1,200 (for a group). The outer-district boutiques like Hop Inn, Mila Garden, Le Park 23 and The Rice suit those with a car more.

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Roi Et hotels include breakfast?
faq.a: The Rice Hotel ฿700 includes breakfast in every room, so it's good value once you factor the morning meal in. Budget stays like Hop Inn and the YaYa Hostel house rental are rooms-only with no breakfast, so you'll eat out (Roi Et has plenty of food around Bueng Phlan Chai). Some M Grand rates also exclude breakfast, so check at booking.

faq.q: ❓ Travelling as a group or family — which budget stay is best value?
faq.a: YaYa Hostel ฿1,200 rents a whole detached house (3 bedrooms, 3 bathrooms, 150 sqm) — split across 5-6 people the per-head cost is very low, and there's a kitchen to cook. For hotel-style service instead, The Premium Residence ฿580 has family rooms and The Rice Hotel ฿700 has Suites with breakfast included.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking budget Roi Et hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion period, so compare all 3 before every booking — 8 of the 9 stays here compare across all three (YaYa Hostel books direct on Agoda). Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night, especially during festivals and long weekends when rates move more.
